originalDescription:
Keep important Excel rows, headings, and columns visible while scrolling with Freeze Panes.

In this TechShift Excel tutorial, we use an Employee Asset Report to demonstrate how to freeze the top row, freeze the first column, freeze a row and column together, freeze multiple rows and columns, and unfreeze the worksheet.

THIS VIDEO COVERS

• Freeze the top row
• Freeze the first column
• Freeze the top row and first column together

• Employee ID
• Employee Name
• Department
• Location
• Employment Status

• Manager
• Email Address
• Laptop Serial
• Asset Status

WHY USE FREEZE PANES?

When you scroll down a long worksheet, the column headings disappear.

When you scroll horizontally, important reference columns such as Employee ID and Employee Name can also disappear.

Freeze Panes keeps the required rows and columns visible while the remaining worksheet continues to scroll.

FREEZE THE TOP ROW

Select:

View → Freeze Panes → Freeze Top Row

This keeps Row 1 visible while scrolling downward.

FREEZE THE FIRST COLUMN

Select:

View → Freeze Panes → Freeze First Column

This keeps Column A visible while scrolling horizontally.

FREEZE THE TOP ROW AND FIRST COLUMN

Select cell B2, then choose:

View → Freeze Panes → Freeze Panes

Excel freezes the row above B2 and the column to the left of B2.

FREEZE MULTIPLE ROWS AND COLUMNS

In our Employee Asset Report:

• Row 1 contains the report title
• Row 2 contains the column headings
• Column A contains Employee ID
• Column B contains Employee Name

To keep Rows 1 and 2 and Columns A and B visible, select cell C3.

Then choose:

View → Freeze Panes → Freeze Panes

Excel freezes every row above the selected cell and every column to its left.

THE RULE TO REMEMBER

Select the cell immediately below the rows and immediately to the right of the columns that you want to keep visible.

UNFREEZE PANES

Select:

View → Freeze Panes → Unfreeze Panes

The worksheet returns to normal scrolling.

Freeze Panes is useful for:

Formula used to return the Employee Name:

=XLOOKUP(G2,A2:A11,B2:B11,"Not Found")

Formula used to return the Department:

=XLOOKUP(G2,A2:A11,C2:C11,"Not Found")

Formula used to return the Laptop Serial Number:

G2 is the Employee ID we want to find.

A2:A11 is the Employee ID range where Excel searches.

B2:B11, C2:C11, or D2:D11 is the information Excel returns.

“Not Found” is displayed when the Employee ID does not exist in the master list.
